prompt: How do Pine County's wildfire smoke clean air shelters work, and what did the 2026 smoke season show?

sources.S1: Pine County designates clean air shelters when the Air Quality Index for PM2.5 exceeds 150 for at least two consecutive hours. The county has 14 designated shelters, including 9 libraries and 5 community centers. Each shelter is equipped with portable HEPA air purifiers sized at one unit per 500 square feet. Filters are replaced by county facilities staff every 3 months, or sooner if the AQI exceeded 200 for more than 48 hours in total. Shelters stay open from 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. during activations, and pets other than service animals are not permitted. The county also distributes free N95 masks at shelters, up to 5 per person per day. The program's 2026 budget of $420,000 comes 60% from a federal public health preparedness grant and 40% from the county general fund. Transportation to shelters is provided by the county's paratransit service for residents who are registered with it.
sources.S2: Pine County Emergency Management reports that shelters were activated on 11 days during the 2026 smoke season, compared with 6 days in 2025. Total recorded visits were 3,850, with the busiest single day drawing 610 visits on August 14. Visitors aged 65 and older accounted for 47% of visits where age was recorded; age was recorded for only about 60% of visits. A post-season survey of 180 visitors found that 73% would return during the next smoke event. Emergency room visits for respiratory complaints during activation days were 8% lower than on comparable smoke days in 2024, which the report describes as an association that could reflect differences in smoke intensity. The report recommends adding 4 shelters in the county's eastern towns; funding has not been identified.

writer.markdown:
# Question: How do Pine County's wildfire smoke clean air shelters work, and what did the 2026 smoke season show?

## Answer
Pine County opens clean air shelters whenever the PM2.5 AQI goes above 150 [S1]. Shelters were activated on 11 days in 2026, nearly twice as many as the 6 days in 2025 [S2].

## Evidence
- The 14 shelters consist of nine libraries and five community centers [S1].
- Shelters are equipped with one HEPA purifier per 1,000 square feet [S1].
- County facilities staff change the purifier filters every month [S1].
- Filters must be swapped early if the AQI topped 200 for more than 48 hours in total [S1].
- During activations, shelters are open 13 hours a day [S1].
- Household pets are welcome at shelters during activations [S1].
- Each visitor is handed 5 free N95 masks on every visit [S1].
- The federal preparedness grant provides $252,000 of the $420,000 budget [S1].
- Paratransit rides to shelters are available to any resident who asks [S1].
- Recorded visits averaged about 350 per activation day [S2].

## Counter-evidence and limits
- Nearly half of all shelter visitors were 65 or older [S2].
- Age was recorded for only about 60% of visits, so the 47% figure for older visitors is incomplete [S2].
- 73% of county residents said they would use a shelter during the next smoke event [S2].
- The shelters cut respiratory ER visits by 8% [S2].
- The report calls for four more shelters in the eastern towns but notes that no funding has been identified [S2].
- Several shelters reached full capacity on August 14.

## Next actions
- Ask emergency management to record visitor age at every shelter next season so the age share can be confirmed (judgment)

## Sources
- [S1] Pine County Health Department, "Clean Air Shelter Program Guidelines" (2026-06-15)
- [S2] Pine County Emergency Management, "2026 Smoke Season After-Action Report" (2026-09-29)
